title: Allah swears by the pen and what it writes.
subtitle: Writing as a gift worth pausing over
then: The surah opens with the letter Nun, whose meaning is known to Allah. Then an oath by the pen. Ibn Kathir says this alerts people to a favor: {reward}Allah taught them writing, and through it knowledge is gained.{/reward} Some early scholars said it also points to {idea}the angels recording every deed.{/idea}
now: You type hundreds of words a day. Messages, notes, comments, a quick reply at midnight. Every one of them is a pen moving. {idea}Somewhere, your deeds are being written too.{/idea} The oath asks you to stop and notice both.
old: Writing is ordinary. Everyone can do it.
new: The ability to write and learn is a gift, and my own record is being written right now.
try: Before you send your next message today, reread it once as if it were going into your record.

title: The one they called mad was the sanest man there.
subtitle: A label from people who refused the truth
then: This is one of the earliest surahs, sent when opposition in Makkah had turned harsh. The chiefs called the Prophet ﷺ insane. Ibn Kathir explains they did this {trap}because they denied the clear truth he brought.{/trap} Allah answers directly: {reward}by your Lord's favor, you are not mad.{/reward}
now: You start praying at work, or stop joining the gossip, and someone says you have gone strange. The family group chat jokes that you have changed. {trap}A label is easier than an argument.{/trap} {idea}It often says more about the one who throws it.{/idea}
old: If people call me strange, maybe I am the problem.
new: When people cannot answer the truth, they label the person carrying it.
try: Think of one label someone gave you for doing right. Let it go with a quiet du'a for them.

title: A reward that never runs out.
subtitle: What patience under insults earns
then: Right after the insult comes the comfort. Ibn Kathir says the reward is for {idea}conveying the message and being patient with their abuse.{/idea} The word means it is {reward}never cut off{/reward}, and Mujahid said it is without reckoning.
now: You care for a sick parent and nobody notices. You keep your temper with a rude customer for the hundredth time. People forget by evening. {reward}Allah's reward for patience does not expire.{/reward}
old: If no one sees my patience, it was wasted.
new: Patience for Allah earns a reward that never stops, seen or unseen.
try: Do one patient thing today that no one will notice, and intend it only for Allah.

title: His character was the Quran, lived out.
subtitle: The answer to their insult was his conduct

row.title: never said uff
sub: ten years of service, Anas said

then: When A'ishah was asked about the character of the Prophet ﷺ, she said: {idea}his character was the Quran.{/idea} Anas served him for ten years and said he {reward}never once said a word of displeasure{/reward} or asked why something was or was not done.
now: Your kid spills juice on the laptop. Your coworker misses the deadline again. The urge is to snap, to say why did you do that. {idea}Ten years and not one uff.{/idea} That is the standard this verse praises.
old: Good character means being nice when it is easy.
new: Great character is living the Quran in the small moments that test you.
try: The next time someone makes a small mistake near you today, skip the why did you. Just help.

title: Wait. Both sides will see clearly soon.
subtitle: Truth does not need to win every argument now
then: The Prophet ﷺ was being mocked daily. Instead of telling him to argue back, Allah says: {idea}you will see, and they will see.{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains it means both he and his opponents {reward}will come to know{/reward} the truth.
now: Someone spreads a false story about you at work. You want to post a long reply tonight and prove everything. {trap}The urge to settle it all right now.{/trap} {idea}Some things are made clear by time and by Allah, not by you.{/idea}
old: If I do not defend myself now, the lie will win.
new: Truth comes out in its time. I can stay calm and keep doing right.
try: Pick one argument you are itching to win. Leave it unsent for 24 hours.

title: The real question: who was truly lost?
subtitle: The accusation turned back on the accusers
then: They said the Prophet ﷺ was the afflicted one. The verse turns the question around. Ibn Kathir says it means they will know {trap}who is insane and misguided{/trap} among them. Like the other verse: {idea}tomorrow they will know who is the liar.{/idea}
now: You are the only one at the table not drinking, or not laughing at the cruel joke. You feel like the odd one. {idea}Being the odd one is not the same as being wrong.{/idea} Ask the real question quietly in your heart.
old: If I am the only one, I must be the one who is off.
new: Being alone with the truth is not madness. Leaving the truth is.
try: Next time you feel like the odd one out for doing right, say silently: Allah knows who is guided.

title: Allah knows best who strayed and who is guided.
subtitle: The final judge of who is right
then: The argument in Makkah was loud. The chiefs had the crowd. This verse closes the matter: {idea}your Lord knows best{/idea} who has gone astray and who is guided. The verdict is {reward}not decided by the majority.{/reward}
now: Likes, views, the comment section, the opinion of your cousins. All of it votes on who you are. {trap}You can spend your life chasing that vote.{/trap} {idea}Only one opinion about your path really matters.{/idea}
old: What people think of me tells me if I am on the right path.
new: Only Allah truly knows who is guided, so His view is the one I live for.
try: Ask Allah once today: guide me, and keep me among those You know are guided.

title: Do not take orders from those who deny the truth.
subtitle: Staying firm when pressure is loud
then: Ibn Kathir links this to the verses before: {reward}just as We favored you with guidance and great character{/reward}, so do not obey the deniers. The surah introduction says the noise around the Prophet ﷺ was {trap}meant to scare him into giving in.{/trap}
now: Friends who laugh at your fasting. A manager who hints that honesty is naive. A feed that tells you faith is old fashioned. {trap}Pressure rarely says obey. It says relax.{/trap} {idea}You do not have to follow it.{/idea}
old: If enough people push, it is easier to just go along.
new: Their pressure does not get a vote over what Allah has given me.
try: Notice one voice today that pushes you away from your faith. Mute it, even for a day.

title: They wanted a deal: you soften, we soften.
subtitle: The quiet trap of compromise on truth
then: The chiefs offered a deal. Ibn Abbas said it meant {trap}you permit our idols, and we permit your religion.{/trap} Mujahid said they wanted him to {trap}be quiet about their gods and abandon the truth.{/trap} The verse names the offer so he would see it clearly.
now: Just skip prayer this once, the meeting is important. Just laugh along, it is only a joke. {trap}Small trades, each one reasonable.{/trap} {idea}Kindness to people is not the same as trading away what is true.{/idea}
old: A little compromise keeps the peace with everyone.
new: I can be gentle with people without bargaining away what is true.
try: Name one small thing you have been softening on to fit in. Decide to hold it this week.

title: The one who swears all the time is weak inside.
subtitle: Why constant oaths are a warning sign
then: The verse begins describing a type of man the people of Makkah knew. Ibn Kathir says the liar, {trap}due to his weakness and disgrace{/trap}, hides behind false oaths using Allah's names, and swears all the time without need. Ibn Abbas said mahin means {trap}the liar.{/trap}
now: I swear, wallahi, on my mother. You hear it in sales pitches and in your own mouth when you are late again. {trap}The more you need oaths, the less your word stands alone.{/trap} {idea}Plain truth needs no swearing.{/idea}
old: Swearing by Allah makes people believe me.
new: A truthful person's plain word is enough. Constant oaths cheapen Allah's name.
try: Go one full day without swearing by Allah in casual talk. Let your yes be yes.

title: He mocks people and carries tales between them.
subtitle: Gossip that breaks good relationships

row.title: corrupting good relations
sub: the Prophet ﷺ warned of it

then: Ibn Kathir explains this man goes around {trap}carrying tales to spoil relations between people{/trap} when they were good. The Prophet ﷺ passed two graves and said one of them was punished for {trap}spreading gossip.{/trap}
now: Did you hear what she said about you? A screenshot forwarded to the wrong chat. A whisper in the office kitchen. {trap}Two people who were fine are now cold.{/trap} {idea}The carrier is part of the damage.{/idea}
old: I only repeated what I heard.
new: Carrying words that break people apart is its own serious wrong.
try: The next time you hear something about someone, let it stop with you.

title: He blocks good, crosses limits, and dives into sin.
subtitle: Three faces of the same hard heart

row.title: I just keep what is mine

then: The description continues. Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}he refuses to give and withholds the good he has{/trap}, he goes beyond the limits even in what is allowed, and {trap}he delves into forbidden things.{/trap}
now: The donation link you scroll past. The help you could give a junior colleague but do not. Telling a friend not to bother volunteering. {trap}Blocking good is quiet. Nobody calls it a sin.{/trap} {idea}The verse does.{/idea}
old: Not giving is not the same as doing harm.
new: Holding back good I could easily give is a real fault, not a neutral choice.
try: Give one small good you have been holding back today: a coin, a kind word, an hour.

title: Harsh, greedy, and known everywhere for his evil.
subtitle: When cruelty becomes what you are known for

row.title: a sheep with a cut ear
sub: easy to spot in the flock

then: Ibn Kathir says 'utul means {trap}cruel, harsh, greedy and stingy.{/trap} Ibn Abbas described a man of Quraysh who stood out for his evil like {trap}a sheep with a piece of its ear cut off.{/trap} The Prophet ﷺ said the people of Paradise are {reward}the weak and humble.{/reward}
now: Think of the person at work everyone warns new hires about. Known for one thing. {trap}Reputations are built one harsh reply at a time.{/trap} {idea}What would people say you are known for?{/idea}
old: Being tough and hard makes people respect me.
new: Harshness marks a person. Humility is what Allah honors.
try: Ask someone close to you, gently: is there a way I come across as harsh?

title: His wealth and sons made him arrogant, not grateful.
subtitle: When blessings become a reason to look down

row.title: I have, so I am above
I have, so I give thanks

then: Ibn Kathir says this is how he responded to {reward}the favors of wealth and children Allah gave him{/reward}: by {trap}disbelieving in Allah's verses and turning away.{/trap} The Quran describes a similar man elsewhere, given plenty and still wanting more.
now: The raise comes through. The kids get into good schools. The house gets bigger. {trap}Slowly you start listening less, to people and to reminders.{/trap} {idea}Every blessing is a test of which way it pushes you.{/idea}
old: I have done well, so I must be on the right track.
new: Wealth and family are gifts that test me, not proof that I am right.
try: List three blessings you have now that you did not have five years ago. Thank Allah for each by name.

title: Old stories, he says, to dodge what the verses ask.
subtitle: Dismissing a reminder instead of hearing it

row.title: legends of old
sub: a lie copied from the ancients

then: When the verses were recited to this man of Makkah, he waved them off. Ibn Kathir says he claimed {trap}they were a lie taken from the tales of the ancients.{/trap} It was easier than facing what they said about his {trap}wealth and pride.{/trap}
now: A friend sends a reminder in the group chat and you think, here we go again. A khutbah touches something real and you file it under old fashioned. {trap}Dismissing is faster than listening.{/trap} {idea}What if it was meant for you?{/idea}
old: I have heard this all before. It does not apply to me.
new: A reminder I am quick to dismiss may be the one I most need.
try: Next time a reminder annoys you, ask: what exactly is it asking me to change?

title: The proud nose will carry a mark everyone can see.
subtitle: What he hid will be made plain

row.title: branded
sub: his matter made clear to all

row.title: it will be made plain
sub: like a mark on the face

then: Ibn Jarir said it means Allah {idea}will make his matter clear so people know him{/idea}, like a brand on an animal. Others said it is {trap}the mark of the people of the Fire on the Day of Judgment.{/trap} The proud face is the very place that is marked.
now: You keep a polished image online. The perfect posts, the careful replies. Behind it, the things nobody sees. {trap}Hidden things have a way of showing.{/trap} {idea}Better to fix them now than have them made plain later.{/idea}
old: As long as nobody sees it, it does not matter.
new: What I hide is not hidden from Allah, and one day it will show.
try: Pick one private habit you would be ashamed to have shown. Take one step away from it today.

title: Makkah was tested like the owners of the garden.
subtitle: A parable about a blessing and a choice

row.title: tested
sub: what will you do with it?

row.title: a test
sub: what you do with it counts

then: Ibn Kathir says this parable is about {reward}the great mercy of sending Muhammad ﷺ{/reward} to Quraysh, who met it with denial. The garden owners {trap}swore at night to harvest early{/trap} so the poor would not know.
now: Your bonus lands. A new job, a healthy baby, a good harvest of any kind. {idea}Each one is a garden and a test.{/idea} The question is what you plan at night about who gets a share.
old: Good things happen to me. Tests are the bad things.
new: Blessings are tests too. What I do with them is the answer.
try: Look at your latest blessing and decide one share of it to give away this week.

title: They made plans without saying if Allah wills.
subtitle: The missing words in a confident plan
then: The owners swore to harvest in the morning, {trap}without saying if Allah wills.{/trap} Ibn Kathir says that because of this, {idea}Allah broke their vow.{/idea} They spoke as if tomorrow was already theirs.
now: I will finish the project by Friday. We are moving next month. He will definitely get the job. {trap}You say it like tomorrow is in your pocket.{/trap} {idea}Two words put it back in Allah's hands.{/idea}
old: If I plan well enough, it will happen.
new: I plan, but tomorrow belongs to Allah. Insha'Allah is honesty, not a habit.
try: Say insha'Allah, meaning it, every time you speak about tomorrow today.

title: While they slept, their garden was already gone.
subtitle: What happens while you are confident and asleep
then: They went to bed with their plan settled. Ibn Kathir says the garden {trap}was struck by a heavenly destruction{/trap} that night. {idea}They were asleep and knew nothing of it.{/idea}
now: You fall asleep with your phone on the charger, calendar full, plans set for the morning. {idea}So much changes in the world while you sleep.{/idea} Your plans were never fully in your hands.
old: My plans are secure because I made them carefully.
new: Everything I count on is held by Allah, even while I sleep.
try: Tonight, before sleeping, hand tomorrow to Allah in your own words.

title: By morning the garden looked like it had been reaped.
subtitle: From full to nothing in one night
then: Ibn Abbas said the garden became {trap}like the dark night.{/trap} Ath-Thawri and As-Suddi said it was {trap}like a crop harvested, withered and dry.{/trap} What took seasons to grow was gone by dawn.
now: A market crashes. A diagnosis arrives. A message ends a friendship. {trap}What took years can change in a morning.{/trap} {idea}It is a reason to hold blessings with open hands and grateful hearts.{/idea}
old: What I have built will always be there.
new: Anything I have can change in a night, so I should thank and share while I can.
try: Thank Allah today for one thing you would hate to lose, and use it well.

title: At dawn they called each other, still sure of their plan.
subtitle: Waking up excited about something already gone
then: Ibn Kathir says in the early morning {idea}they called each other to go together{/idea} and pick the harvest. They had no idea {trap}what had happened in the night.{/trap}
now: You wake up and message the team: let us go, big day. Full of energy for the plan. {trap}We are often most sure right before the surprise.{/trap} {idea}Humility in the morning costs nothing.{/idea}
old: I know exactly how today will go.
new: I start each day not knowing what Allah has already decreed for it.
try: Start tomorrow's first message or call with bismillah, said with attention.

title: Go early, they said, before anyone else can come.
subtitle: Rushing so no one else gets a share
then: Go early to your crop, they said. Ibn Kathir explains the whole plan was to pick the fruit {trap}so the poor and the beggars would not know{/trap}, and they could {trap}keep it all and give none in charity.{/trap}
now: You order delivery after the kids are asleep so you do not have to share. You leave the office quietly so no one asks for a lift. {trap}Small timing tricks to avoid giving.{/trap} {idea}The plan reveals the heart.{/idea}
old: Being early and smart is just good planning.
new: Planning to avoid giving is not smart. It is the garden owners' mistake.
try: Notice one small way you dodge sharing. Do the opposite once today.

title: They whispered, but Allah heard every word.
subtitle: Secret plans are not secret from Allah

row.title: Allah
sub: and He told us what they said

then: They walked and spoke in low voices so no one could hear. Ibn Kathir notes that {idea}Allah, the Knower of secrets and private talks{/idea}, then revealed exactly what they whispered. {trap}The hidden plan was told in the Quran for all time.{/trap}
now: The private chat. The DM you would never want screenshotted. The plan you only say behind a closed door. {idea}Allah hears it all, the same as if it were shouted.{/idea}
old: What I say in private stays private.
new: Allah hears my whispers as clearly as my words in public.
try: Read back your last private conversation. Would you be comfortable with Allah reading it? He has.

title: Not one poor person gets in today.
subtitle: The exact words that cost them everything
then: Ibn Kathir reports one account that their father used to {reward}give the excess of the harvest in charity.{/reward} When he died, the sons said he was foolish, and if they {trap}kept the poor out, they would have more.{/trap}
now: Your parents always had an extra plate for whoever dropped by. Now you count every cost and think that was naive. {trap}Closing the door feels like good management.{/trap} {idea}Sometimes the generous habit was the blessing itself.{/idea}
old: If I stop giving, I will have more for myself.
new: Shutting out the poor does not protect my wealth. It can be what removes it.
try: Keep one good habit of giving you inherited from a parent or elder, or restart it this week.

title: They marched out sure they had full control.
subtitle: Confidence in your own power
then: Ibn Kathir says they went {trap}with strength and power{/trap}, and they {trap}thought they had the power to do what they wanted.{/trap} They felt fully in charge of something that was no longer there.
now: You walk into the meeting with the deal already signed in your head. You budget the money before the contract arrives. {trap}Confidence can slide into thinking you control the outcome.{/trap} {idea}Prepare, then hold the result loosely.{/idea}
old: I have the skill and resources, so I control the result.
new: My effort is mine. The outcome is Allah's.
try: Before your next big task, pause and say: Allah, I did my part, the result is Yours.

title: This cannot be our garden. We must be lost.
subtitle: The first reaction is denial
then: When they arrived, the garden had gone {trap}from luster and abundance to black and empty.{/trap} Ibn Abbas said they first thought {idea}they had taken the wrong path.{/idea} It could not be theirs.
now: The bank balance. The test result. The message from the school. Your first thought: that cannot be right, there must be a mistake. {idea}Denial is the first step before facing what happened.{/idea}
old: This cannot be happening to me.
new: When loss comes, the first honest step is to admit it is real.
try: Name one hard thing you have been refusing to look at. Look at it, with a du'a.

title: No, this is ours. We have been deprived.
subtitle: The moment denial turns into the truth
then: Ibn Kathir says they changed their minds and {idea}realized it was the right path after all.{/idea} Then they said: {trap}this is it, but we have no portion and no share.{/trap} They had planned to deprive the poor. They were the ones deprived.
now: You held back from helping your sister with rent, and then the car broke down for the same amount. {trap}What you keep from others does not always stay with you.{/trap} {idea}Not as a rule to calculate, but as a reason to reflect.{/idea}
old: Holding back from others keeps more for me.
new: Depriving others can leave me the one deprived.
try: Think of someone you have been holding back from helping. Help them in one small way today.

title: The fairest brother said: did I not tell you?
subtitle: The one voice that tried to stop them

row.title: glorify Allah
sub: say if Allah wills, give thanks

then: The early scholars said the awsat was {reward}the most just and the best of them.{/reward} He had warned: why do you not glorify Allah? Mujahid said it meant {idea}why do you not say if Allah wills?{/idea} Others said it meant thank Allah for His favor.
now: There is usually one person in the group who says, maybe we should not. The colleague who asks if this is honest. The cousin who says, let us include them. {idea}Be glad of that voice. Or be that voice.{/idea}
old: The one who objects is just slowing everyone down.
new: The quiet voice reminding us of Allah is often the wisest one in the room.
try: Next time a group plan feels wrong, say one calm sentence about it.

title: Glory to our Lord. We were the wrongdoers.
subtitle: Admitting the wrong, though late

row.title: before the loss
sub: when it can still change things

then: They finally said what the best brother had asked for. Ibn Kathir notes {trap}they became obedient when it was of no benefit to the garden{/trap}, and confessed when it could not save it. Still, {idea}they named their wrong honestly.{/idea}
now: You apologize to your friend only after they stop answering. You start praying only when the hospital calls. {trap}Waking up late is still waking up.{/trap} {idea}But earlier is always better.{/idea}
old: I will fix things when something forces me to.
new: Saying I was wrong to Allah now is better than saying it after the loss.
try: Say one honest sentence to Allah today about a wrong you have not admitted yet.

title: Then they turned on each other with blame.
subtitle: After the loss, the finger pointing
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}they started blaming each other{/trap} for what they had decided: keeping the poor from their right to the fruit. In the end their answer to one another was only to {idea}confess the error together.{/idea}
now: The project fails and the team chat fills with who said what. A family plan goes wrong and every sibling has a version. {trap}Blame feels like relief, but it fixes nothing.{/trap} {idea}Owning your part does.{/idea}
old: If I can show it was someone else's idea, I am clear.
new: If I went along with a wrong, I own my part of it.
try: Think of a recent group mistake. Say to one person: my part in it was this.

title: Woe to us. We went beyond every limit.
subtitle: Seeing how far you crossed the line

key.label: How it felt vs what it was

then: Ibn Kathir explains they meant: {trap}we transgressed, trespassed and exceeded the bounds{/trap} until this happened to us. What felt like a smart plan the night before {idea}now looked like what it really was.{/idea}
now: At the time it was just one small shortcut on the tax form, one harsh word to your child. Later you see it whole. {trap}Limits are often crossed one step at a time.{/trap} {idea}Seeing it clearly is the start of coming back.{/idea}
old: It was only a small step over the line.
new: Small crossings add up, and naming them honestly opens the way back.
try: Name one line you have been slowly crossing. Step back from it once today.

title: Perhaps our Lord will give us something better.
subtitle: Hope right after the loss

row.title: hope in Allah
sub: He can replace it with better

then: The story ends with the brothers {reward}turning to their Lord in hope.{/reward} Ibn Kathir says some said they hoped for {reward}a better garden in this life{/reward}, others said for its reward in the Hereafter. And Allah knows best.
now: You lost the job, the deal, the friendship, and part of it was your fault. The voice in your head says it is over. {reward}The door to Allah is still open.{/reward} {idea}Regret that turns to hope is the right kind.{/idea}
old: I messed up. There is no coming back from this.
new: After a loss I caused, I can still turn to Allah and hope for better.
try: Make one du'a today asking Allah to replace something you lost with something better.

title: This is the worldly loss. The next one is greater.
subtitle: The parable's lesson for everyone listening
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}such is the punishment of whoever opposes Allah's command and is stingy{/trap} with what Allah gave him. The surah introduction says Makkah was being told: {idea}you too have been tested like the garden owners.{/idea}
now: Losing money hurts. Losing a business hurts more. {trap}But some losses are bigger than anything on a bank statement.{/trap} {idea}The story is told so you can choose differently while there is time.{/idea}
old: The worst thing that can happen is losing what I have here.
new: Worldly loss is a warning. What truly matters is the Hereafter.
try: Give something today from what you love most, as a small step for the Hereafter.

title: The mindful have gardens with their Lord that never wither.
subtitle: The other garden, after the lost one
then: Right after the garden that was destroyed, Allah mentions another. Ibn Kathir says those with taqwa {reward}will have Gardens of Delight in the Hereafter that will never end{/reward}, and {reward}their pleasures will never cease.{/reward}
now: You scroll past homes, holidays, gardens that seem perfect. All of them can vanish in a night. {reward}There is a garden that will not.{/reward} {idea}It is built by being mindful of Allah.{/idea}
old: The good life is the one I can see and touch now.
new: The garden that lasts is with Allah, and taqwa is how I reach it.
try: Do one act today purely out of mindfulness of Allah, with the lasting garden in mind.

title: Would Allah treat the obedient and the criminals the same?
subtitle: Justice means different outcomes for different paths

row.title: surely not
sub: by the Lord of heaven and earth

then: The chiefs of Makkah assumed they would do fine whatever happened. Ibn Kathir explains the question: {idea}should We deal equally between them in recompense?{/idea} His answer: {trap}nay, surely not.{/trap}
now: The honest worker and the one who cheats get the same bonus. The kind sibling and the cruel one get the same praise. {trap}It can feel like goodness does not count.{/trap} {idea}With Allah, it always counts.{/idea}
old: Good or bad, it all ends up the same in the end.
new: Allah is just. Obedience and wrongdoing do not end in the same place.
try: Do one good deed today that nobody will reward you for, trusting that Allah sees it.

title: What is wrong with you? How can you judge this way?
subtitle: Questioning a comfortable assumption
then: After asking if the obedient and the criminals are equal, Allah asks the deniers directly: what is the matter with you? Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}how can you think that?{/idea} {trap}Their confidence had no ground.{/trap}
now: I am a good person, I will be fine. You hear it, and maybe you say it. {trap}A feeling dressed as a certainty.{/trap} {idea}The verse asks: on what basis?{/idea}
old: I am basically good, so I do not need to worry.
new: My hopes about the Hereafter need a real basis, not just a feeling.
try: Write down one assumption you have about your standing with Allah. Ask what it rests on.

title: Do you have a scripture that says you can do anything?
subtitle: Asking for the source of a claim
then: Ibn Kathir explains Allah is asking: {idea}is there in your hands a Book sent from heaven{/idea} that you study and memorize and pass on through the generations, {trap}containing the laws you claim?{/trap} They had nothing of the kind.
now: It is fine, everyone does it. Allah will understand. You make up a rule because it suits you. {trap}A private scripture written by your wishes.{/trap} {idea}The question is fair: where does it say that?{/idea}
old: I know Allah would be fine with this.
new: If I claim something about Allah, I should be able to show where it comes from.
try: Pick one religious thing you say often. Check its source this week.

title: A book promising you whatever you choose?
subtitle: The fantasy of getting everything you want
then: The challenge continues: does your book say {trap}you shall have all that you choose?{/trap} The chiefs acted as if {trap}their wishes were guaranteed.{/trap} Ibn Kathir shows there was no such book.
now: Some ads promise that you deserve it all. Some talks promise that if you want it enough, it is yours. {trap}A world where wanting equals having.{/trap} {idea}The Hereafter does not work by wishes.{/idea}
old: If I want it badly enough, I will get it.
new: My outcome is not what I choose but what Allah judges by my deeds.
try: Replace one I deserve thought today with I hope, Allah willing.

title: Did Allah swear an oath to give you what you decide?
subtitle: No one holds a contract over Allah
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}do you have covenants and confirmed agreements with Us{/trap}, that you will attain all you want and desire? The chiefs acted as if Allah had signed a deal with them. {idea}He had not.{/idea}
now: I pray, so my business should succeed. I fasted, so my exam should go well. {trap}Quietly turning worship into a contract.{/trap} {idea}Allah is generous, but He is not bound to my terms.{/idea}
old: I have done my part, so Allah has to give me what I asked.
new: Allah owes me nothing. Everything He gives is generosity.
try: Make one du'a today that ends with: but You know what is best for me.

title: Ask them who will guarantee that claim.
subtitle: A bold claim needs someone to stand behind it
then: The Prophet ﷺ is told to ask them directly. Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}who is the sponsor who guarantees this?{/idea} Ibn Abbas said it means {idea}which of them will be guarantor for that?{/idea} {trap}None of them could be.{/trap}
now: Someone tells you not to worry about prayer, nobody will ask about it. Ask them: will you answer for me on that Day? {trap}Easy advice costs the giver nothing.{/trap} {idea}You are the one who carries it.{/idea}
old: If enough people say it is fine, it must be fine.
new: No one who reassures me can stand in my place before Allah.
try: When someone tells you a wrong is fine, ask yourself quietly: will they answer for me?

title: Their partners? Let them bring them, if truthful.
subtitle: Testing what you rely on besides Allah
then: Ibn Kathir explains the question: {trap}do they have idols and rival gods besides Allah?{/trap} If so, {idea}let them bring them, if they are truthful.{/idea} The idols of Makkah could not answer the call.
now: Your savings, your boss's favor, your follower count, the doctor you trust. {trap}Things we lean on as if they could save us.{/trap} {idea}Ask each one: can you help me on the Day?{/idea}
old: I have people and things that will back me up.
new: Nothing I rely on besides Allah can stand for me when it matters most.
try: Name one thing you lean on too heavily. Thank Allah for it, and remind yourself who provides it.

title: On that Day, some will try to bow and cannot.
subtitle: The call to prostrate on the Day of Judgment
then: Ibn Kathir says this is the Day of Judgment, with its great terrors. The Prophet ﷺ said {reward}every believing man and woman will prostrate to Allah{/reward}, and those who {trap}prostrated in this life only to be seen{/trap} will try and be unable.
now: You pray quickly at the office so no one notices, or slowly at the masjid so someone does. {trap}Who is the prostration for?{/trap} {idea}The sujood you make sincerely now is the one you will be able to make then.{/idea}
old: As long as I pray, why I pray does not matter much.
new: Sincere prostration now is what I carry into that Day.
try: In one prayer today, make your sujood a little longer, for Allah alone.

title: They were called to bow while they were healthy.
subtitle: The chance that was there all along
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}when they were called to prostrate in this life, they refused{/trap}, even though {reward}they were healthy and secure.{/reward} So they were met with the opposite of what they did.
now: Your knees work. Your back bends. The adhan plays on your phone and you swipe it away. {reward}Right now prostration is easy.{/reward} {idea}Being sound is an invitation, not a given.{/idea}
old: I will get serious about prayer when I am older.
new: My health right now is the window to bow while it is easy.
try: Pray the next prayer on time, and thank Allah for the body that lets you do it.

title: Leave them to Me. I lead them on step by step.
subtitle: When ease is not always a blessing

row.title: gradual drawing in
sub: from where they do not know

row.title: it may be a test
sub: check what you do with it

then: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ to leave the deniers to Him. Ibn Kathir explains that they {trap}believe it is a noble blessing from Allah{/trap}, but it is drawing them on gradually. Elsewhere: {idea}do they think the wealth and children We give them is Us hastening good?{/idea}
now: Everything is going right. The promotion, the house, the health. And your prayer is getting thinner, your reminders fewer. {trap}Comfort can quietly lull you.{/trap} {idea}Ease is a time to check yourself, not relax.{/idea}
old: If life is easy, Allah must be pleased with me.
new: Ease can be a test. What I do with it shows the truth.
try: In a good week, add one extra act of worship as thanks, not wait for a hard week.

title: I give them time, and My plan is firm.
subtitle: Delay is not the same as escape
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah delays them and extends their time. The Prophet ﷺ said {idea}Allah gives respite to the wrongdoer until He seizes him{/idea}, and then {trap}he will not escape.{/trap} He then recited the verse about Allah seizing towns.
now: Nothing bad happened after you lied. The harsh words to your parents went unanswered. {trap}It is easy to think it did not count.{/trap} {idea}The time you have now is a gift to turn back.{/idea}
old: Nothing happened, so it must not have mattered.
new: If Allah has given me time, it is time to repent, not proof I escaped.
try: Think of one wrong that has gone unpunished. Use today to make it right.

title: Did he ever ask them for payment?
subtitle: A message given freely, still refused
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {reward}you, O Muhammad ﷺ, call them to Allah without taking any wages{/reward}, hoping for reward from Allah. {trap}Yet they reject what you brought out of ignorance, disbelief and obstinacy.{/trap}
now: Your grandmother asks you to pray. A friend sends a free lecture link. Nobody is selling you anything. {trap}And still it is easy to push it away.{/trap} {idea}Advice given for free often has the purest intention.{/idea}
old: People who preach must want something from me.
new: Sincere advice that asks nothing in return deserves a real hearing.
try: Thank one person who gave you sincere advice for free, and act on a piece of it.

title: Do they hold the unseen and write it down?
subtitle: Claiming to know what only Allah knows
then: Ibn Kathir notes this verse was explained in Surat At-Tur. The deniers spoke as if {trap}the unseen was in their hands to write down.{/trap} The Prophet ﷺ asked nothing of them, and still {trap}they rejected out of obstinacy.{/trap}
now: I know I have time. I know it will work out. I know they will never change. {trap}We talk about the future like we have read it.{/trap} {idea}Only Allah has.{/idea}
old: I know how my life will turn out.
new: The unseen belongs to Allah. I act today and leave tomorrow to Him.
try: Notice one I know for sure about the future today. Change it to Allah knows.

title: Be patient, and do not leave in anger like Yunus.
subtitle: Waiting for Allah's decision without walking away
then: Ibn Kathir says the Prophet ﷺ was told to {idea}persevere against the harm and rejection of his people.{/idea} Yunus had {trap}gone off angry with his people{/trap}, was swallowed by the fish, and called from the darkness: {reward}none has the right to be worshipped but You.{/reward}
now: The family that never listens. The job where nothing changes. The urge to slam the door and leave. {trap}Anger makes leaving feel like the answer.{/trap} {idea}Patience waits for Allah's decision.{/idea}
old: When people do not listen, I am done with them.
new: Patience waits for Allah's decision instead of storming off.
try: The next time you want to walk out angry, say la ilaha illa Anta, subhanaka, and wait.

title: Only his Lord's favor reached him in time.
subtitle: Grace that catches you after a mistake
then: Ibn Kathir quotes another surah: {reward}We answered his call and delivered him from the distress, and thus We deliver the believers.{/reward} Had he not been one who glorified Allah, {trap}he would have stayed in the belly of the fish.{/trap}
now: You made the bad call. You said the thing you cannot unsay. You feel like you are in the dark. {reward}Allah's favor can still reach you there.{/reward} {idea}The way out begins with turning to Him.{/idea}
old: My mistake was too big for me to be saved from it.
new: Allah's favor reaches the one who turns to Him, even from the darkest place.
try: In a moment of stress today, say the du'a of Yunus once, slowly.

title: Then his Lord chose him and made him righteous.
subtitle: A slip is not the end of the story
then: After the fish, {reward}his Lord chose him and made him of the righteous.{/reward} The Prophet ﷺ said {idea}it is not befitting for anyone to say I am better than Yunus bin Matta.{/idea}
now: Someone at the masjid knows your past. Your family remembers the old you. {trap}People keep you in your worst chapter.{/trap} {idea}Allah lifts the one who turns back.{/idea}
old: Once I have failed, that is who I am.
new: When I turn back to Allah, He can raise me higher than before.
try: Stop retelling one old failure of someone else's today. Let them be who they are now.

title: Their glares were full of hate, but Allah protected him.
subtitle: Jealous eyes and the insult of madness
then: Ibn Kathir says their glares came from {trap}jealousy and hatred{/trap}, and only {idea}Allah's protection{/idea} kept him from harm. When a man admired another and harm followed, the Prophet ﷺ said: {reward}if you see something you like in your brother, pray for blessing for him.{/reward}
now: Your friend posts the new house, the engagement, the promotion. Something tight rises in your chest. {trap}Envy looks before it speaks.{/trap} {idea}Turn it into a du'a for them instead.{/idea}
old: Feeling a little jealous of others is harmless.
new: When I admire what someone has, I can turn it into a prayer for their blessing.
try: Next time you see someone's good news, say barakallahu lak, out loud or in your heart.

title: It is nothing but a reminder for all the worlds.
subtitle: The surah ends where it began: the truth of the message
then: The surah opened with the charge of madness and ends with the answer. The surah introduction says the Book he brought was itself {idea}enough to refute their accusations.{/idea} It is not madness. {reward}It is a reminder to all the worlds.{/reward}
now: The Quran app on your phone. The verse a friend sent this morning. The recitation in the car. {reward}A reminder meant for you, today, in your city.{/reward} {idea}Not just for people long ago.{/idea}
old: The Quran was mainly a message for people back then.
new: The Quran is a reminder for every world, and that includes my life now.
try: Read one short passage of the Quran today and ask: what is this reminding me of?
